hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try $6(x + 5)$ first: it expands to $6x + 30$. This problem only changes the $x$ term to $2x$.
The $6$ multiplies both terms in the parentheses. Some of the wrong choices skip one of them.
Work out $6 \cdot 2x$ and $6 \cdot 5$, then look for the choice with both of those products.
$6 \cdot 2x = 12x$ and $6 \cdot 5 = 30$, so the equivalent expression is $12x + 30$, choice B.

explanation: Distribute the $6$ to each term inside the parentheses.
The first product is $6 \cdot 2x = 12x$, which comes from $6 \times 2 = 12$.
The second product is $6 \cdot 5 = 30$, a plain number.
Together they give $12x + 30$, which is choice B.
